groups.title: Oral liquid (158603ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 bottle (100 mg as iron) once a day. Children aged 12 years to under 19 years: take 1/2 bottle (50 mg as iron) at a time, 2 times a day. Children aged 1 year to under 12 years: take 1/2 bottle (50 mg as iron) at a time, 1 to 2 times a day. Take the dose before a meal, during a meal or after a meal.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which abnormal iron metabolism causes iron to be deposited in the liver and pancreas), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, impaired iron utilisation, iron overload, anaemia due to bone marrow failure, chronic haemolytic anaemia, iron deficiency anaemia caused by infection or a tumour, chronic pancreatitis or liver cirrhosis.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis, impaired cardiac or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney impairment or low blood protein.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with iron-containing preparations (iron supplements, liver contrast agents for MRI and the like), anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene, diphosphonates, thyroxine, cefdinir preparations, quinolones, penicillamine, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, vitamin E preparations, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If hives, itching, skin hypersensitivity on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, coma, occasional rises in AST and ALT, rare rises in ALP, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, discoloration of the teeth or stomach discomfort appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E04800ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are debilitated or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Ointment (170947COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the eczema and dermatitis group of conditions, for itchy skin and for insect bites.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 3 times a day; the amount is increased or decreased as appropriate according to symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a skin infection (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, shingles, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice); if you have eczematous otitis externa with a perforated eardrum; if you have an ulcer (except in Behçet's disease); if you have a deep second-degree or worse burn or frostbite; if you have perioral dermatitis, common acne or rosacea; or if the user is a young child under 2 years of age.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is a baby, a young child or an older person, or if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or have had a reaction to it.

Do not use this medicine in the eyes. Do not use it for purposes other than treatment, such as after applying make-up or shaving. Do not use an occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision. Limit treatment with this medicine to no more than 7 days.

If impetigo, folliculitis, candidiasis, ringworm, boils, skin irritation, stinging, fever, a burning feeling, rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, prickly heat, sweat rash, worsening of a wound, pressure sores or pustulosis appears, or if raised eye pressure or glaucoma (blurred vision) occurs when it is used on the skin of the eyelids, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Because of absorption into the body, reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, Cushing's syndrome, high blood sugar, sugar in the urine, visual disturbance and blurred vision of unknown frequency may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (187203ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the antacid action and the improvement of symptoms in excess stomach acid, gastroduodenitis and gastritis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (0.5 to 1 g) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day, on an empty stomach. The dose is increased or decreased as appropriate according to age or symptoms.
groups.caution:
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have liver impairment, impaired heart function or high blood magnesium.

Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine together with tetracycline antibiotics.

Occasionally, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, constipation, thirst or itching may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (136603ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve mild to moderate pain from muscle pain, neuralgia, injury and surgery, headache, toothache and earache.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1/2 to 1 tablet (125 to 250 mg) at a time, 3 times a day.
groups.caution:

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a history of peptic ulcer; if the user is a child or an older person; if you have high blood pressure, fluid retention or heart failure; if you have bronchial asthma; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; or if you are breast-feeding.

While taking this medicine, do not take it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, ACE inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor antagonists, aspirin, diuretics, lithium, methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (warfarin and the like), ciclosporin and tacrolimus, antiplatelet medicines and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), or corticosteroids. If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal pain, bleeding in the digestive tract, peptic ulcer and perforation, or — rarely — shock, rash, itching, anaemia, raised AST and ALT, drowsiness, headache, dizziness, cold sweat, chills or abnormal euphoria appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you need to restrict sodium strictly, for example because of congestive heart failure or kidney impairment; if you have high blood calcium, nephrocalcinosis or recurrent calcium-containing kidney stones; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 7 days of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

When taking this medicine with tetracycline, digoxin, fluoroquinolones, iron salts, ketoconazole, neuroleptics, thyroxine, penicillamine, beta-blockers (atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), glucocorticoids, chloroquine, estramustine or diphosphonates, leave an interval of 2 hours between them.

If itching, bronchial constriction or an allergic reaction appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 1 to 2 tablets at a time, when needed, at intervals of 6 hours. Do not take more than 6 tablets in total in one day. Children under 12 years of age must not take this medicine.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had an asthmatic reaction to this medicine or to another cold medicine or antipyretic analgesic, if the user is a child under 12 years of age, or if you are already taking another medicine that contains acetaminophen.

groups.title: Capsule (E02100ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule at a time. Take the dose 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had an allergic reaction to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, swelling, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain, ulcer or bleeding problems; if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or cannot absorb fluid; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with diuretics or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide), medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding in the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, hearing loss, swelling, ringing in the ears, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, impaired liver function (general lassitude, jaundice and the like), interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever and the like), pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine output, swelling of the face and limbs, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache and the like) or myopathy (weakness, cramp of the arms or legs, paralysis and the like) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (D66200ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent and relieve the dizziness, vomiting and headache caused by motion sickness.
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 1 1/2 sachets (15 mL) at a time. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 1 sachet (10 mL) at a time. To prevent motion sickness, take a dose 30 minutes before boarding a vehicle or a boat. If a further dose is needed, take one dose leaving an interval of at least 4 hours.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake.

Do not take this medicine if you are breast-feeding, or if the user is a baby or young child under 3 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms from this medicine (rash, reddening of the skin, itching and the like); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; or if you have a respiratory disease such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other analgesics, cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, or external preparations containing an antitussive or expectorant. Avoid alcoholic drinks while taking this medicine.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching or thirst appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to chlorzoxazone; if you have had hypersensitivity symptoms (rash, reddening of the skin, itching, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips); or if you have had asthma when using another cold medicine or antipyretic analgesic.
